chunks: First: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

A man who bequeathed to his slave one-third of his wealth, he (the Imam) said: The slave is valued at his price, then it is seen what is one-third of the deceased's estate. If it is less than the value of the slave by the amount of a quarter of the value, the slave is extended (paid) in a quarter of his value. And if it is more than the value of the slave, the slave is freed and what remains of the third after the value is given to him.
Second: As for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from one of the Imams (peace be upon him)

He said: 'There is no bequest for the slave.' This report carries two meanings: One is that there is no bequest for a slave from those other than his masters; as for from his master, it is valid. The other aspect is that the intended meaning of the report is that it is not permissible for the slave to bequeath because he owns nothing and his wealth is his master's wealth.
Third: What Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said regarding the slave: As long as he is a slave, he and his wealth are for his family (master). It is not permissible for him to befreed, nor to give much gift, nor to bequeath, unless his master wishes.

key_terms.ثُلُثُ الْمَالِ: One-third of the wealth (portion for bequests)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a slave's bequest in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes seemingly contradictory reports by distinguishing between a slave's capacity to own property (which allows for valid bequests) and the procedural mechanics of deducting the slave's valuation from the one-third estate share. This analysis highlights the Shia juristic principle that while a slave's wealth is technically the master's, the master's consent or specific conditions determine the validity and execution of the slave's testamentary dispositions.
